title: A Tryouts for the Recipe
premise: Dominic Coldharbour has spent three years keeping his family invisible—until a card in Grandma Marisol's recipe box, labeled 'Stew for Winning,' turns out to be a working spell. The recipe box is a relic of the Ledger, a hidden society that settles grievances outside courts and police, and its annual Championship decides who holds the Ledger's power for a generation. When the Coldharbours are pulled into the tryouts by a rival faction who wants the box destroyed, Dominic discovers his mother has been secretly serving the Ledger for years to keep a corrupt magistrate, Aldous Vane, from seizing their grandmother's seat. To save the family, Dominic must win both the school's meaningless culinary championship—his cover for training—and the true Championship of the Ledger, exposing Vane's corruption and choosing to share power rather than hoard it, before the final card in the box burns out on the last night of the season.
about_author: Juniper Ravensworth is a former line cook who grew up in a household held together by casseroles and stubbornness. She writes stories about ordinary kids who find extraordinary doors in ordinary kitchens.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A day in the Coldharbour household: packing lunches, covering for twelve-year-old Pia's skipped class, dodging questions about Mom's night shifts at the hospital. Dominic's rules for survival are laid out—never stand out, never owe anyone, never open Grandma's box. Beat: love expressed as vigilance, and the ache of being a parent at seventeen.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't a Recipe
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hunting for a birthday dinner idea, Dominic finally opens the recipe box and finds a card titled 'Stew for Winning' with instructions that read like a ritual—salt on the doorstep, names spoken backward. When he half-follows it as a joke, the kitchen lights gutter and a brass token materializes in the pot. Beat: wonder cracking through exhaustion.

chapters.title: Pia Sees It First
chapters.summary: Pia's POV. Pia, sharp-eyed and starved for magic in her grey life, catches the token glowing and blackmails Dominic into testing another card. The 'Bread for Courage' recipe makes little brother Milo fearless enough to face the bullies who took his backpack. Beat: the siblings become co-conspirators, and belonging begins at home.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Farmers Market
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A stranger named Odile Corvane recognizes the token at the market and warns Dominic to burn the box before 'the Ledger' finds it—then vanishes when a black car idles past. That night, an engraved summons appears inside the box: the Coldharbour name has been entered in the tryouts. Beat: fear that the family's invisibility is gone for good.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Job
chapters.summary: Mom's POV (interleaved with Dominic). Dominic follows Mom's bus route and watches her slip into a basement office where robed figures weigh grievances on antique scales. He learns she's been a Ledger 'clerk' since Grandma Marisol died, hiding her service to keep Vane from claiming the family's vacant seat. Beat: betrayal and pride tangled together.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Ledger tryouts are disguised as the regional youth cooking championship—a perfect cover. Dominic, Pia, and Milo are assigned a mentor, the sardonic Odile, who reveals Vane has rigged the bracket so the Coldharbours fail publicly, invalidating Marisol's seat. Beat: the stakes sharpen—lose and the family loses its protection.

chapters.title: Salt and Shortcuts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Training montage with a cost: every spell-recipe works, but each one draws on the cook's memory. Milo forgets his best friend's name after a confidence card; Dominic starts losing small memories of his father. Beat: power always takes payment, and Dominic must decide what he's willing to spend.

chapters.title: The Rival with the Familiar Face
chapters.summary: Pia's POV. The opposing team's captain, Cass Vane, turns out to be Aldous Vane's daughter—and Pia's estranged former best friend. Cass offers Pia a place on the winning side, promising the Ledger will 'take care' of her family better than Mom's night shifts ever have. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Round One: What You Can Prove
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. First official round: contestants must cook a dish that proves a truth about themselves, judged by the scales. Dominic's honest, unmagical dish scores higher than his spelled one—the scales weigh sincerity, not power. Beat: first victory, and the discovery that the Ledger's old law still has honor in it.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Aldous Vane corners Dominic with a velvet-glove threat: withdraw, and the Ledger will erase the family's debts; refuse, and Mom's clerical fraud will be prosecuted by the mundane courts. He shows Dominic the ledger page with Mom's signature. Beat: the trap of justice that only protects the powerful.

chapters.title: What Mom Signed
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Mom confesses everything at the kitchen table: she falsified the succession record after Marisol's death to keep the seat from Vane, believing the family's magic could shield them. Dominic, furious, realizes his mother's lies and his own rule-following are two versions of the same fear. Beat: the family's first fully honest conversation in years.

chapters.title: Round Two: The Memory Course
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The second round requires cooking from memory—literally. Contestants sacrifice memories as ingredients, and Vane's team burns through stolen memories harvested from debtors. Odile reveals she once lost her own daughter's face to a Championship recipe. Beat: grief as testimony; the corruption is older and bigger than one villain.

chapters.title: Cass Defects, Almost
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass finds her father's harvest vault—jars of memories taken from families like the Coldharbours—and brings the evidence to Pia, then wavers when Vane threatens to erase her memories of her late mother. Beat: the cost of conscience, and a fragile alliance between the rivals.

chapters.title: The Burned Card
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Someone ransacks the house and burns half the recipe box; the final card, 'Feast for the Turning of Power,' is missing. Odile is attacked and hospitalized, whispering that the Championship's true prize is the box itself—the Ledger's founding instrument. Beat: despair, and Dominic's decision to stop playing defense.

chapters.title: Round Three: Cooking for the Accused
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The semifinal doubles as a public trial: each team cooks a 'grievance dish' for a real complainant. Dominic and his siblings cook for a family Vane dispossessed, using the last intact cards to restore a fragment of their stolen memories. Beat: justice outside the law, performed in front of witnesses—the crowd begins to turn.

chapters.title: The Scales Tip
chapters.summary: Mom's POV. Vane retaliates by filing charges against Mom in both worlds. She chooses to surrender herself to the Ledger's court rather than flee, gambling that an honest confession before the scales will expose Vane's pattern of coercion. Beat: courage as accountability; the mother models what she asks of her son.

chapters.title: What the Box Is For
chapters.summary: Dominic and Pia's alternating POV. Decoding Grandma Marisol's annotations, they learn the box was built by the Ledger's founders to hold power in trust for the powerless—and that Vane can only claim it by winning the final round 'cleanly.' The final card reconstitutes from the burned ashes, but only if cooked by all three siblings together. Beat: hope rebuilt on family as the unit of power.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The mundane culinary championship final runs the same day as the Ledger's. Dominic, exhausted, cooks a plain family stew—no magic—and wins the school trophy to thunderous, oblivious applause. Beat: a breath of ordinary joy, and proof of who Dominic is when nothing supernatural is at stake.

chapters.title: Final Round: The Feast for the Turning of Power
chapters.summary: All three siblings' POV, braided. In the Ledger's great hall, the Coldharbours cook the reconstituted card against Vane, who cheats with the harvest vault. The scales reject his dish—built on stolen memories—and accept the siblings' stew, seasoned with a memory each of them freely gave: Milo's fearlessness, Pia's grudge, Dominic's memory of his father's voice. Beat: the climax—power turned by willing sacrifice.

chapters.title: Vane Unmasked
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. With the scales' verdict public, the harvested memories return to their owners mid-hall. Cass testifies against her father; the Ledger's clerks, including a freed Mom, vote to strip Vane's seat and dissolve his faction. Beat: justice as restoration, not punishment—and Cass choosing the harder, better family.

chapters.title: The Seat at the Table
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Offered Marisol's seat, Dominic refuses to hold it alone: he installs a rotating council of clerks, complainants, and former debtors, with Mom as the first elected chair. Odile recovers and takes the mentor's post; the recipe box goes into the council's shared trust. Beat: power shared is power that doesn't corrupt.

chapters.title: Stew for Winning
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. Months later: homework on the table, Mom home before midnight, Cass at the counter arguing recipe ratios with Pia, Milo teaching Odile's daughter card games. Dominic cooks the original, unmagical 'Stew for Winning' and finally adds his own card to the box—written in pencil, meant for ordinary dinners. Beat: belonging achieved not by winning, but by being fully seen.
